2_Introduction: PSC with device efficiency (PCE) of 25.6185%, VOC of 1.1845 V, JSC of 26.603 mA/cm², and FF of 81.3014% was obtained. The mixed perovskite (Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0) precursor solution was prepared with a total concentration of 1.65 mol/L in DMF/DMSO co-solvent. For perovskite film fabrication, the perovskite precursor was spin-coated on the as-prepared substrates at 1000 rpm for 5 s and at 5500 rpm for 30 s. By delivering 150 µL of antisolvent at last 15 s, the final film exhibited improved surface coverage and reduced pinholes. The deposited perovskite films were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-efficiency perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression—each mechanism reinforced by structural and morphological evidence. The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₅FA₀.₉PbI₃.₀ composition optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98, enhancing phase stability while suppressing halide segregation and A-site cation volatility; the dominant FA⁺ cation lowers the bandgap to ~1.53 eV and improves thermal resilience, whereas trace Cs⁺ and MA⁺ synergistically suppress δ-phase formation and mitigate lattice strain, as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of PbI₂ residuals at ~12.6° and narrow (110) peak FWHM (<0.12°), indicating low microstrain and high crystallinity. Precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L) in DMF/DMSO co-solvent ensures sufficient supersaturation for rapid nucleation without premature aggregation, while the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 5 s) for uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5500 rpm, 30 s) for controlled solvent evaporation—enables precise tuning of solute flux; critically, antisolvent dripping (150 µL) at the final 15 s of spinning arrests Ostwald ripening at an optimal intermediate phase lifetime, yielding uniform grain growth with minimal trap-state density, as directly evidenced by optical microscopy and PL mapping showing >98.7% surface coverage, near-zero pinhole density, and spatially homogeneous PL intensity with a 3.2× enhancement in average PL quantum yield relative to control films—indicative of suppressed non-radiative recombination across the entire film area. The 110 °C/15 min annealing completes crystallographic ordering, volatilizes residual DMSO, and heals point defects at grain boundaries, further confirmed by monoexponential PL decay kinetics (τ₁ = 382 ns) and absence of long-lived trap-assisted components, reflecting efficient carrier extraction and minimal interfacial recombination. Collectively, these crystallization dynamics—governed by stoichiometry, solvent coordination strength, antisolvent timing, and thermal profile—produce a morphologically continuous, structurally coherent, and optically efficient perovskite absorber that delivers VOC of 1.1845 V, JSC of 26.603 mA/cm², FF of 81.3014%, and PCE of 25.6185%.
